name: Otar Iosseliani
teaser: Georgian-born director of wordless, comic observations of everyday life, exiled from the USSR after criticizing its film bureaucracy.

exploreAction.targetName: Falling Leaves (1966) — any 25-minute stretch
exploreAction.instruction: Watch the faces of the workers on the tea plantation. Iosseliani finds whole novels in a glance.

name: Sergei Parajanov
teaser: Armenian-born visual poet whose tableaux of folklore and faith are among the most image-dense films ever made. He painted with people.

exploreAction.targetName: The Color of Pomegranates (1969) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Forget plot. Read the film like a museum wall of living icons — each shot is a painting that moves a little.

name: Andrei Konchalovsky
teaser: Russian-born director who moved between Soviet epics, Hollywood, and intimate dramas, always chasing big themes through small lives.

exploreAction.targetName: Siberiade (1979) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how a Siberian village tracks a century of Russian history. Konchalovsky films the land as memory.

name: Ermanno Olmi
teaser: Italian humanist who filmed workers, farmers, and drifters with documentary patience, finding sacredness in ordinary labor.

exploreAction.targetName: The Tree of Wooden Clogs (1978) — the first 40 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how Olmi lets a full season pass without drama. Life's rhythm is the movie; the clogs are the symbol.

name: Maren Ade
teaser: German director of excruciatingly truthful social comedies — office hierarchies, family road trips, and the unbearable weight of expectations.

exploreAction.targetName: Toni Erdmann (2016) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch the awkwardness build in real time. Ade holds her scenes long enough for embarrassment to become love.

name: Matteo Garrone
teaser: Italian director who moves between Naples crime stories and dark fairy tales with the same anthropological eye for how people survive.

exploreAction.targetName: Gomorrah (2008) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Notice what's missing: no heroes, no score, no glamour. The mafia is filmed like a factory's shift report.

name: Ciro Guerra
teaser: Colombian director who films the Amazon and the coast as characters — hypnotic voyages where myth and exploitation share a canoe.

exploreAction.targetName: Embrace of the Serpent (2015) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch the black-and-white jungle double with a color version decades later. Guerra films colonialism as a river you travel twice.

name: Marco Bellocchio
teaser: Italian rebel of the 1960s who made explosive films about family, faith, and madness, still working six decades later.

exploreAction.targetName: Fists in the Pocket (1965) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how a family dinner becomes a chamber of psychological warfare. Bellocchio's debut never softens.

name: Ettore Scola
teaser: Italian director of bittersweet ensemble comedies that hid social history inside jokes — a restaurant table becomes a century of Italy.

exploreAction.targetName: We All Loved Each Other So Much (1974) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how three friends' lives interleave across decades. Scola cuts between their fates like a deck of cards.

name: Gillo Pontecorvo
teaser: Italian director of the anticolonial classic The Battle of Algiers, so real it was once used by the Pentagon for training.

exploreAction.targetName: The Battle of Algiers (1966) — the first 40 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch it like news footage — that's the point. Pontecorvo rebuilt a revolution with non-professionals and documentary grammar.

name: Francesco Rosi
teaser: Italian director who invented the investigative thriller — films that use the camera like a prosecutor building a case against the powerful.

exploreAction.targetName: Salvatore Giuliano (1962) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Notice how the film starts with the death and works backwards. Rosi wants you to investigate, not just watch.

name: Liliana Cavani
teaser: Italian director of provocative philosophical films — The Night Porter asked whether victims and perpetrators can ever really separate.

exploreAction.targetName: The Night Porter (1974) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Hold the discomfort. Cavani is testing where complicity begins and whether memory can ever be escaped.

name: Maria Luisa Bemberg
teaser: Argentine director who came to film at fifty and made pointed period dramas about women trapped by the era they were born into.

exploreAction.targetName: Camila (1984) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch a forbidden love against a repressive state. Bemberg films defiance as a private, costly act.

name: Mario Monicelli
teaser: Italian master of commedia all'italiana who showed the poor laughing through misery — a comedian with a sociologist's eye.

exploreAction.targetName: Big Deal on Madonna Street (1958) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch a heist planned by people who can't even be trusted to hold a torch. Monicelli's genius is failing with style.

name: Luigi Comencini
teaser: Italian director of warm, precise films about children and the poor — often dismissed as gentle, often hiding real anger.

exploreAction.targetName: Bread, Love and Dreams (1953) — any 25-minute stretch
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how comedy and social observation share the same scenes. Comencini makes poverty funny without mocking it.

name: Arturo Ripstein
teaser: Mexican director of dark, still melodramas about family rot and desperation — Buñuel approved of him, which says almost everything.

exploreAction.targetName: Principio y Fin (1993) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how a family unravels in measured, gloomy steps. Ripstein films ruin the way others film romance.

name: Pablo Larraín
teaser: Chilean director who makes psychological portraits of public figures — Pinochet, Jackie Kennedy, Diana — as haunted interior dramas.

exploreAction.targetName: No (2012) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how the film itself looks like a 1988 TV broadcast. Larraín uses the medium of advertising to end a dictatorship.

name: Sebastián Lelio
teaser: Chilean director of precise, empathetic portraits of women breaking free — from a Jehovah's Witness housewife to a trans rock star.

exploreAction.targetName: Gloria (2013) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch the dance floor scenes. Lelio lets a middle-aged woman be joyful, awkward, and alive without a single cruel joke.

name: Patricio Guzmán
teaser: Chilean documentarian who spent forty years filming his country's memory — first the coup, then the landscape that holds it.

exploreAction.targetName: Nostalgia for the Light (2010) — the first 30 minutes
exploreAction.instruction: Watch how astronomers and the mothers of the disappeared share the same desert. Guzmán films memory itself.

name: Miguel Littín
teaser: Chilean director who returned to Pinochet's Chile in disguise to make a secret film about his own country — a story Gabriel García Márquez wrote down.

exploreAction.targetName: Acta General de Chile (1986) — any 30-minute stretch
exploreAction.instruction: Watch it knowing the crew filmed under false identities. Every street scene is an act of resistance.

name: Ida Lupino
teaser: Actress turned director who in 1949 became one of Hollywoods only female filmmakers, tackling rape, polio, and bigamy in hard little noirs.

exploreAction.targetName: The Hitch-Hiker (1953) — end to end
exploreAction.instruction: Watch the only classic noir directed by a woman. Lupino strips the thriller to two men and a killer in a car.
